CausalChain: Oxidative stress in liver cells → (induces) Nrf2 dissociation from Keap1 → (phosphorylated) p62 binds Keap1 → Autophagic degradation of Keap1 → Enhanced Nrf2 nuclear translocation → Upregulation of cytoprotective antioxidant genes → Suppression of hepatic stellate cell activation → Attenuation of liver fibrosis
Hypothesis: Selective pharmacological enhancement of p62 phosphorylation in hepatic stellate cells will promote Keap1 degradation and trigger controlled Nrf2 activation, thereby reducing oxidative stress and fibrogenesis in the liver without engendering the oncogenic risks associated with chronic, non-specific Nrf2 hyperactivation.
Abstract: We propose a novel therapeutic strategy aimed at attenuating liver fibrosis by exploiting the interplay between selective autophagy and Nrf2‐mediated antioxidant defense. In this approach, the targeted enhancement of p62 phosphorylation in hepatic stellate cells promotes the autophagic degradation of Keap1. This event facilitates controlled Nrf2 activation leading to enhanced transcription of antioxidant and detoxification genes. Furthermore, such modulation may reduce the activation of hepatic stellate cells that drive extracellular matrix deposition and fibrogenesis, while potentially avoiding the sustained and systemic hyperactivation of Nrf2 that has been linked to tumorigenic metabolic reprogramming.
